title: Freya and the Oath
premise: Ansel Oyelaran, a bone-carver who hears the voices of the dead, has spent years guiding smugglers through the Thornfell mountains while hiding their gift from the Crown's witch-finders. When a century-old prophecy book surfaces naming tonight's date and a stranger named Freya, the two are thrown together by royal soldiers hunting both of them. Freya, it turns out, is the prophesied Unbinding — the only person who can free King Aldric from the hollow thing that took his crown and wears his face — but doing so requires breaking an oath Ansel swore to the dead of Thornfell. As the false king's hunters close in and the dead grow louder, Ansel must choose between the oath that kept them safe and the love that makes them whole; in the end they unbind the true king at the cost of their own hearing, silencing the dead forever, and choose Freya and their found family over the lonely gift.
about_author: Casper Vane is the pen name of a former cartographer who once mapped smuggling routes through real mountain passes before trading ink for fiction. They write fantasy about people caught between promises, and claim to have never met a ghost they didn't argue with.

chapters.title: The Date That Wasn't Tomorrow
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. In their mountain workshop, Ansel carves a memorial bone for a drowned child while the dead murmur their usual grievances. A peddler sells them a water-stained prophecy book; flipping through it, Ansel finds tonight's date circled and their own name beside a stranger's. The emotional beat is quiet dread — the dead have never lied to Ansel, and neither does paper.

chapters.title: Freya Falls Out of the Sky
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya, a disgraced royal archivist fleeing the capital with pages torn from the prophecy book, is cornered on the Thornfell road by witch-finders. Ansel, guiding a smuggler caravan, pulls her into a hidden pass only the dead know. The beat is reluctant alliance: she needs a guide, he needs answers, neither trusts the other.

chapters.title: What the Dead Remember of Kings
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Sheltering in a smuggler's cave, Ansel reads the prophecy aloud: an Unbinding will free a king from 'the thing wearing his crown.' The dead of Thornfell react violently — one voice, an old queen's, screams that the crown was stolen twice. Freya reveals the true King Aldric hasn't been seen in three years. Beat: the stakes sharpen from escape to mission.

chapters.title: The Oath at Thornfell Bridge
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, flashback woven into present. We learn why Ansel hears the dead: as a child they swore an oath at the mass grave of a massacred village — carry our names, never serve the Crown — in exchange for the gift. Now the prophecy demands they approach the Crown itself. Beat: the central conflict crystallizes; love versus duty begins its long argument.

chapters.title: Witch-Finders at the Waystation
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. At a mountain waystation, witch-finders led by Captain Serah Voss nearly catch them; a smuggler found-family member, old Marta, covers their escape and is taken instead. Freya realizes her archive theft painted a target on everyone who helps her. Beat: guilt, and the first proof that this found family bleeds for strangers.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Reaching the lowland city of Carrowmere, they witness the false king hold court: Aldric's body moves, smiles, signs decrees — but his shadow doesn't match him, and birds refuse to land on the palace. Ansel hears, from miles away, a faint human voice screaming inside the crown. Beat: horror confirmed; the enemy is not a man but a hunger.

chapters.title: Names for Sale
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. To enter the palace they need forged papers; Ansel trades a favor to the smuggler network — led by charming fence Odile and her crew of orphans and exiles. The found family theme deepens: these outlaws keep better faith than any court. But Odile warns that helping them means defying the Crown openly. Beat: warmth shadowed by cost.

chapters.title: The Queen in the Bone
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The old queen's voice among the dead finally speaks clearly: she was Aldric's grandmother, murdered by the same entity generations ago when it first tried to take the throne. It cannot be killed, only unbound — separated from its host by someone who owes it nothing and loves its victim. Beat: revelation that reframes the prophecy as a love story.

chapters.title: What Freya Tore From the Archive
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya confesses why she fled: she discovered the Crown knew about the entity and had been feeding it prisoners to keep it docile. Her mentor died for the knowledge. She isn't the prophesied hero by destiny — she chose this. Beat: vulnerability; Ansel sees her fully for the first time, and something shifts between them.

chapters.title: Voss Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Captain Voss's POV (brief interlude). Voss, herself bound by an oath to the Crown, tracks them through Carrowmere's undercity. She captures Odile's youngest runner and offers a trade: Freya for the child. Beat: the antagonist gains dimension — she believes law is the only thing standing against chaos, mirroring Ansel's oath.

chapters.title: The Trade That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The exchange goes wrong: Voss planned betrayal, but the smuggler network planned better. In the chaos, Ansel takes a witch-finder's iron blade meant for Freya. Wounded, feverish, Ansel hears the dead more clearly than ever — including, impossibly, a living voice: King Aldric, begging from inside his own skull. Beat: sacrifice cements the bond.

chapters.title: Fever Dreams and Older Promises
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Nursing Ansel in a safehouse, Freya keeps vigil while Ansel deliriously relives the massacre oath. The dead press close, demanding Ansel honor the vow by walking away from the Crown's business entirely. Freya realizes loving Ansel may mean helping them break the prophecy — or watching the oath consume them. Beat: tenderness entangled with dread.

chapters.title: The Road Under the Mountain
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Recovered, they take the deepest smuggler road — beneath Thornfell itself, past the mass grave where the oath was sworn. There, the dead rise as presence rather than voice and offer Ansel a terrible bargain: abandon the king, and the voices will finally fall silent. Beat: temptation at its most seductive; duty and desire invert.

chapters.title: Marta's Cell
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya infiltrates the witch-finder garrison to free Marta and finds Voss interrogating her — and discovers Voss's own family name appears in the prophecy book as a past failed Unbinding. Voss lets Freya go, shaken. Beat: enemy becomes question mark; the reader learns oaths can be inherited wounds.

chapters.title: Assembly of the Broken
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, anchored by Odile. The smugglers, the freed Marta, a defecting witch-finder clerk, and the two protagonists gather in Odile's warehouse to plan the impossible: get Ansel and Freya into the throne room during the Feast of the Founding, when the entity must surface fully to renew its hold. Beat: found family becomes a war council; hope with teeth.

chapters.title: The Feast of the Founding
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Disguised as archive clerks, they enter the palace mid-feast. Up close, the false king is worse than rumor: courtiers orbit him like moths, eyes glazed, slowly being drained. Ansel, hearing hundreds of fading voices, falters — and the entity turns its head and looks directly at them. It knows what they are. Beat: terror at the threshold.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing His Crown
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Captured and brought before the entity, Ansel is offered everything: silence for the dead, safety for Freya, if they walk away. The entity shows them the massacre — revealing the Crown ordered it, and the oath was sworn against a lie Ansel built their life on. Beat: devastating midpoint-of-the-end crisis; identity shattered.

chapters.title: Breaking the Oath
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. In a dungeon cell, the dead themselves release Ansel: the oath was meant to protect the powerless, and keeping it now serves the powerful. Ansel formally breaks it — and chooses, freely, to still hear them. Freya breaks them out with Voss, newly turned, holding the door. Beat: catharsis; duty transformed from chain to choice.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating Ansel and Freya POV. In the throne room, Freya performs the archive rite while Ansel anchors Aldric's mind with the sound of his grandmother's voice carried through bone. The entity tears free, screaming, and Voss — last of her failed line — gives her life to seal it beneath the mountain. Beat: climax; love and justice outside the law win at real cost.

chapters.title: A King, Quietly Restored
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Aldric wakes diminished but himself, horrified by what was done in his name. He offers Ansel and Freya titles, pardons, a place at court. They decline — mostly. Justice must be done for the fed prisoners and the massacred village, and they intend to oversee it from outside the palace walls. Beat: resolution of the power question; refusal as integrity.

chapters.title: The Silence After
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Back in Thornfell, Ansel discovers the price of the Unbinding: the dead are gone, truly gone — the workshop silent for the first time in their life. Grief and relief arrive together. At the mass grave, they carve one final bone bearing every name, no longer needing to hear them to remember. Beat: mourning the gift that was also a wound.

chapters.title: Freya and the Oath
chapters.summary: Shared POV, closing chapter. Spring comes to the mountain. The found family gathers at the rebuilt waystation — Odile's crew, Marta, a visiting king incognito. Ansel, teaching Freya the smuggler roads, realizes the prophecy never made them heroes; choosing each other did. Final beat: an open door, a shared future, and an oath remade as a promise between equals.
